semantic_correction.stem: During newborn discharge teaching, a parent asks how to prepare the infant's sleep area at home. Which parent statement demonstrates correct understanding?

options.A: Place the infant on the back for every sleep on a firm, flat crib or bassinet mattress with only a fitted sheet.
options.B: Place the infant on the side in the crib and use a rolled blanket behind the back to help maintain the position.
options.C: Place the infant on the stomach in a firm, flat crib after feeding and remove pillows, blankets, and soft toys.
options.D: Place the infant on the back on an adult bed with pillows and blankets removed while a caregiver remains nearby.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current CDC infant safe-sleep guidance recommends placing babies on their backs for all sleep times, using a firm and flat sleep surface such as a mattress in a crib or bassinet covered by a fitted sheet, and keeping soft bedding and soft objects out of the sleep area. Option A follows these core recommendations. Side sleeping is not the recommended sleep position and adding a rolled blanket introduces soft bedding; prone sleeping is not recommended for routine infant sleep; and an adult bed is not an appropriate infant sleep surface even if pillows and blankets are removed. The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan places newborn and infant education, postpartum/newborn discharge teaching, and preventive health education within Health Promotion and Maintenance. Therefore A is the uniquely best answer.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach caregivers to place an infant on the back for every sleep on a firm, flat crib or bassinet surface with only a fitted sheet and without soft bedding or soft objects.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: retired an HCAHPS/performance-improvement item because it tested managerial quality-data interpretation and duplicated an already cleaned QI cluster. Rebuilt the UID into direct newborn discharge teaching on infant safe sleep using current CDC guidance and explicit NCSBN newborn/infant education content.

audit_findings_append.finding: The replacement tests a direct preventive teaching decision. CDC supports back sleeping, a firm flat sleep surface and removal of soft bedding; NCSBN directly includes newborn/infant education and newborn discharge instructions.

scope_exclusions.room_sharing_duration: No room-sharing duration is tested, avoiding age-duration precision that is not necessary to the construct.
scope_exclusions.swaddling: No swaddling recommendation or discontinuation milestone is tested.
scope_exclusions.temperature_or_clothing: No room-temperature target, sleep-clothing recommendation, or overheating threshold is asserted.
scope_exclusions.medical_exceptions: The item concerns routine safe sleep for a healthy infant and does not generalize positioning for infants with a specific medically directed exception.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub search for 'infant safe sleep back firm flat surface no blankets pillows' returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank rescan was performed.

option_audit.A: Correct. It combines the CDC-supported supine position, firm flat infant sleep surface, fitted sheet, and absence of soft bedding.
option_audit.B: Plausible positioning misconception, but side sleeping is not recommended and the rolled blanket adds soft bedding to the sleep area.
option_audit.C: Plausible because the crib surface is firm and soft objects are removed, but routine prone sleeping conflicts with the recommendation to place infants on the back for every sleep.
option_audit.D: Plausible because the infant is supine and soft bedding is removed, but an adult bed is not the recommended infant sleep surface.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. B uses side positioning plus soft bedding, C uses prone positioning, and D uses an adult bed. A alone satisfies the complete core safe-sleep pattern supplied by CDC.

cueing_check.note: Exact character counts were calculated from the stored strings. All four alternatives are effectively identical in length and use parallel sleep-placement actions.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: NCSBN Health Promotion and Maintenance explicitly includes newborn/infant care and education, newborn discharge instructions, preventive care education and evaluation of caregiver ability.
